summary: Block 4. Integrated Astra's review. Lemma A independently verified (repo proof in AUDIT.md Sec.9): for any K-invariant mu (no ergodicity) and z != 0, |a_z| = 1 forces mu = delta_trivial, since span_Z K = E, the constants assemble into a homomorphism, so mu is a point mass, and -1 = (r-1)+(s-1) kills it. Hence a wild mu has |a_z| < 1 for every nonzero z, so the coset-supported counterexample branch is closed, not merely stalled. Corrections accepted: ann(z) is not K-stable (no quotient action); C meets a coset in countably many parallel lines; the uncentered Avg|a(uz-z)|^2 is the wrong object (it tends to |a_z|^4 and equals 1 at z=0) - the correct criterion M3 uses centered characters and coincides with weak mixing; first-stage properness does not give terminal properness. One targeted finite-character argument tested: it PROVES M3 implies diagonal ergodicity (Stone-Weierstrass density plus finitely many pairs, no Haar, no tower), and its remaining gap is exactly a uniform deficit (U) for coefficients a_{z-u^{-1}z'} along K-orbits, which pointwise strictness cannot supply. Also shown: constant-modulus eigenfunctions with nontrivial eigenvalue must NOT be excluded (witness on T^2), so the target is invariant functions only. No tower claims; no builds.
verified_results: [verified here] Lemma A (Astra): for K-invariant mu and z != 0, |a_z| = 1 => a_z = 1 and mu = delta_{1_D}; so wild mu has |a_z| < 1 for all z != 0. Proof chain checked step by step: span_Z K = E via t = n(u+v); Cauchy-Schwarz equality; K-countability; homomorphism of constants; mu = delta_{d_0}; K-invariance kills (K-1)E; (r-1)+(s-1) = -1 with r = (1+sqrt3 i)/2; hence trivial. One compressed step in Astra's writeup (identifying the constants c_u = c) needed the homomorphism step first; repaired.
[verified here] u . ann(z) = ann(uz), so ann(z) is K-stable only if Z uz = Z z for all u in K, false: no quotient action on D/H_z.
[verified here] C cap (a . ann(z)) = union over k in Z of {xi : xi.(Re z, Im z) = theta_0 + 2 pi k}, countably many parallel affine lines, not one line.

[verified here] with h_z = psi_z - a_z and a_{uz} = a_z: <U_u h_z, h_w> = a_{uz-w} - a_z conj(a_w). So M3 is the centered criterion and it vanishes identically if z = 0 or w = 0. The uncentered Avg|a_{uz-z}|^2 is wrong: it tends to |a_z|^4 and equals 1 at z = 0.

[proved here] M3 implies mu x mu is ergodic under the diagonal action: for invariant F with mean 0 and norm 1, take a finite character polynomial G with ||F-G|| <= eta and mean 0; invariance gives ||U G - G|| <= 2 eta for all u, while M3 makes avg_u ||U G - G||^2 -> 2||G||^2 >= 2(1-eta)^2. Uses only Stone-Weierstrass density and M3 at finitely many pairs; no Haar orthogonality, no compact tower.

[proved here] the target must be restricted to nonconstant INVARIANT functions: Z acting on T^2 by (R_alpha, R_beta) with 1, alpha, beta Q-independent is ergodic on the diagonal, yet F = psi_1 tensor psi_1 is a nonconstant eigenfunction of modulus 1 with eigenvalue exp(2 pi i (alpha+beta)) != 1. So constant-modulus eigenfunctions with nontrivial eigenvalue coexist with ergodicity and must be tolerated.

[proved here] the exact failure point of the finite-character argument: with G = sum_z psi_z tensor f_z, the u-dependence is entirely in lambda_{z,z'}(u) = a_{z-u^{-1}z'}, and a contradiction needs a uniform deficit (U): for every finite Z and delta_0 there are delta > 0 and a density-1 set of u with |a_{z-u^{-1}z'}| <= 1 - delta. Lemma A gives only pointwise strictness, and at z = u^{-1}z' the coefficient is a_0 = 1, so no strictness holds there. (U) implies M3 strictly, so it is a harder statement than the paper's own Sec.3.
conjectures: M3 holds for the paper's wild mu (equivalently (D,mu) is weakly mixing), but proving it looks strictly harder than needed: the paper's Theorem 2.3 is a stronger conclusion reached by different means, and (W-style) routes through pointwise strictness are closed.

A cheaper substitute for M3 would be a decay statement only for pairs (z,w) that arise from a finite character approximant of a hypothetical invariant function, with the deficit allowed to depend on the approximant's frequency window; that weaker form may be provable from PD/positivity constraints alone. Untested.

escalation.obstacle: M3 (equivalently weak mixing of a wild law) is the exact hypothesis the compact-tower simplification needs, and the only route from Astra's pointwise strictness |a_z| < 1 to M3 is the uniform deficit (U), which is strictly stronger than M3. No counterexample exists any more (Lemma A closed the coset branch), so this is a proof gap, not a consistency problem.
escalation.definitions: E = F(i), F = Qbar cap R, discrete; K = {u in E : |u| = 1}; D = E-hat; a_z = int psi_z dmu; (M3) for all z,w: avg_{u in Phi_n} |a_{uz-w} - a_z conj(a_w)|^2 -> 0 along a fixed Følner sequence; (U) for every finite Z and delta_0 there are delta > 0 and D subset K of upper Banach density 1 with |a_{z - u^{-1}z'}| <= 1 - delta for all u in D, z != z' in Z.
escalation.attempted: point spectrum / coset support (closed by Lemma A); uncentered Fourier decay (wrong object); finite-character approximation (proves M3 => ergodicity, cannot prove M3); uniform deficit (U) from pointwise strictness (no mechanism).
escalation.expected_useful_output: Either a positivity-based proof of a uniform deficit for the finite frequency configurations that an invariant-function approximant produces (which would prove the simplification and let Sec.2.4 and Sec.3.1 be deleted), or a precise statement of the finite configuration a counterexample must realise, which is then a finite search problem rather than an ergodic-theoretic one.
